title: Forklift fuel, batteries, lighting and loading docks study guide
description: Study guide on forklift fuel storage, battery charging and changing, lighting, carbon monoxide, dockboards, trucks and railroad cars (29 CFR 1910.178(f)-(k)).
intro: 29 CFR 1910.178 is OSHA's general industry standard for powered industrial trucks. This guide sets out what paragraphs (f) through (k) state on fuel handling and storage, changing and charging storage batteries, lighting for operating areas, control of noxious gases and fumes, dockboards (bridge plates), and highway trucks, semitrailers and railroad cars. These paragraphs are short, so the guide has fewer points than others. goraedu does not train, evaluate or certify operators, and this is not a certification exam. Your State may run its own OSHA-approved plan with its own rules, so check them too. Every point links to the regulation and quotes its exact words.

topics.name: Fuel handling and storage

points.text: Under 1910.178(f)(1), the storage and handling of liquid fuels such as gasoline and diesel fuel shall be in accordance with NFPA No. 30-1969, which the rule incorporates by reference as specified in § 1910.6.
points.quote: The storage and handling of liquid fuels such as gasoline and diesel fuel shall be in accordance with NFPA Flammable and Combustible Liquids Code (NFPA No. 30-1969), which is incorporated by reference as specified in § 1910.6.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Under 1910.178(f)(2), the storage and handling of liquefied petroleum gas fuel shall be in accordance with NFPA No. 58-1969, also incorporated by reference as specified in § 1910.6.
points.quote: The storage and handling of liquefied petroleum gas fuel shall be in accordance with NFPA Storage and Handling of Liquefied Petroleum Gases (NFPA No. 58-1969), which is incorporated by reference as specified in § 1910.6.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

notCovered: The content of NFPA No. 30-1969 and NFPA No. 58-1969 is not described here; 1910.178(f) only names them.

points.text: Battery charging installations shall be located in areas designated for that purpose.
points.quote: Battery charging installations shall be located in areas designated for that purpose.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: 1910.178(g)(2) says facilities shall be provided for flushing and neutralizing spilled electrolyte and for fire protection.
points.quote: Facilities shall be provided for flushing and neutralizing spilled electrolyte, for fire protection,

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The same paragraph also requires facilities for protecting charging apparatus from damage by trucks, and for adequate ventilation for dispersal of fumes from gassing batteries.
points.quote: for protecting charging apparatus from damage by trucks, and for adequate ventilation for dispersal of fumes from gassing batteries.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Smoking shall be prohibited in the charging area.
points.quote: Smoking shall be prohibited in the charging area.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Precautions shall be taken to prevent open flames, sparks, or electric arcs in battery charging areas.
points.quote: Precautions shall be taken to prevent open flames, sparks, or electric arcs in battery charging areas.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Tools and other metallic objects shall be kept away from the top of uncovered batteries.
points.quote: Tools and other metallic objects shall be kept away from the top of uncovered batteries.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For handling batteries, one of the options named shall be provided: a conveyor, an overhead hoist, or equivalent material handling equipment.
points.quote: A conveyor, overhead hoist, or equivalent material handling equipment shall be provided for handling batteries.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Reinstalled batteries shall be properly positioned and secured in the truck.
points.quote: Reinstalled batteries shall be properly positioned and secured in the truck.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For handling electrolyte, one of the options named shall be provided: a carboy tilter or a siphon.
points.quote: A carboy tilter or siphon shall be provided for handling electrolyte.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: When charging batteries, acid shall be poured into water; water shall not be poured into acid.
points.quote: When charging batteries, acid shall be poured into water; water shall not be poured into acid.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Before anyone attempts to change or charge batteries, the truck shall be properly positioned and the brake applied.
points.quote: Trucks shall be properly positioned and brake applied before attempting to change or charge batteries.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Care shall be taken to assure that vent caps are functioning.
points.quote: Care shall be taken to assure that vent caps are functioning.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The battery (or compartment) cover(s) shall be open to dissipate heat.
points.quote: The battery (or compartment) cover(s) shall be open to dissipate heat.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.name: Lighting, gases and dockboards

points.text: Where general lighting is less than 2 lumens per square foot, auxiliary directional lighting shall be provided on the truck.
points.quote: Where general lighting is less than 2 lumens per square foot, auxiliary directional lighting shall be provided on the truck.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Concentration levels of carbon monoxide gas created by powered industrial truck operations shall not exceed the levels specified in § 1910.1000.
points.quote: Concentration levels of carbon monoxide gas created by powered industrial truck operations shall not exceed the levels specified in § 1910.1000.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For dockboards (bridge plates), 1910.178(j) does not set its own rule; it refers to subpart D of this part.
points.quote: Dockboards (bridge plates). See subpart D of this part.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

notCovered: The carbon monoxide levels in § 1910.1000 and the dockboard rules in subpart D are not set out here.

topics.name: Highway trucks, semitrailers and railroad cars

points.text: The brakes of highway trucks shall be set and wheel chocks placed under the rear wheels to prevent the trucks from rolling while they are boarded with powered industrial trucks.
points.quote: The brakes of highway trucks shall be set and wheel chocks placed under the rear wheels to prevent the trucks from rolling while they are boarded with powered industrial trucks.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: To prevent railroad cars from moving during loading or unloading operations, one of the options named shall be provided: wheel stops or other recognized positive protection.
points.quote: Wheel stops or other recognized positive protection shall be provided to prevent railroad cars from moving during loading or unloading operations.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: When a semitrailer is not coupled to a tractor, the rule says fixed jacks may be necessary to support it and prevent upending during the loading or unloading.
points.quote: Fixed jacks may be necessary to support a semitrailer and prevent upending during the loading or unloading when the trailer is not coupled to a tractor.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Positive protection shall be provided to prevent railroad cars from being moved while dockboards or bridge plates are in position.
points.quote: Positive protection shall be provided to prevent railroad cars from being moved while dockboards or bridge plates are in position.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)
